sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the Everyday English Podcast series. I'm Emily and today I will
teach you how to speak English at an auction. An auction is a place where different items
or services are sold and people place bids to buy them. You can find artwork, collectibles,
houses, cars, and even celebrity items at auctions. If you are attending an auction for
the first time, the process might seem a bit confusing. How do you register? How do you
place a bid? Why does the auctioneer speak so fast? Don't worry. In this episode, I will
teach you some essential English phrases and dialogues that you can use at an auction.
Let's get started.
1. Registering for an auction. Before you can place a bid, you need to register for the
auction. There is usually a registration desk where you must show your ID and sometimes
pay a deposit. Useful English phrases for registering. Hello, I'd like to register for
the auction. What do I need to do to bid? Do I need to pay a deposit? Can I get a bidding
number? When does the auction start? Is there an online bidding option? Example dialog. Hello,
I'd like to register for the auction. Sure, please fill out this form and show your ID.
Do I need to pay a deposit? No, but you need to collect a bidding number.
Tip. Some auctions require online registration in advance, so always check before you go.
2. Viewing the items for sale. Many auctions allow participants to preview the items before
bidding begins. You may want to ask questions about the condition, history, or authenticity
of an item. Useful phrases for viewing items. Can I take a closer look at this item? What
original piece? Has this item been restored? What year was this made? Is there a minimum bid?
Excuse me. Can I take a closer look at this painting? Auction staff? Of course,
this is an original piece from 1890. What is the starting bid? The bidding starts at $500.
Tip. Most auctions have a catalog listing all items for sale.
Reading the catalog beforehand can help you prepare.
3. Understanding the auction process. During an auction, the auctioneer speaks very fast
and uses special terms. Here are some important words you need to know. Auction terms.
Starting bid, the initial price of an item. Bid to place an offer for an item. Going once,
going twice, sold. The auctioneer's final call before selling an item. Reserve price,
the minimum price the seller is willing to accept. Hammer price, the final price at which
an item is sold. Paddle bidding number. A number assigned to each bidder.
Example auctioneer speech. We're starting this painting at $500. Do I hear $600? $600
to the lady in red? $700? Yes! 800s, going once, going twice, sold for $700.
Tip if the auctioneer speaks too fast, focus on the numbers and decide when to place your bid.
Placing a bid. If you want to buy an item, you can raise your paddle or place a verbal bid.
Useful phrases for bidding. I'd like to bid $100. I'll go up to $200. I want to increase my bid.
I'm out of the bidding. Example dialogue. I'd like to bid $500. We have $500. Do I hear $600?
I'll go up to $600. Tip, don't let emotions take over. Some people get too competitive and bid
more than they planned. 5. Paying and collecting your item. If you win the bid,
you need to pay for your item and arrange for collection. Useful phrases for payment
and collection. How do I pay for my item? Can I pay by credit card? Do you offer shipping?
Example dialogue. Hello, I won the painting for $700. How do I pay? You can pay by card or cash.
And that's it. Today, you learned how to speak English at an auction.
Goodbye.
